title: This is How Pros Draft Reality Fracture!!! (ft. @LordsofLimited)
player_note: NicolaiBolas drafts (his name is on the banner); the guest Ethan Sack (Lords of Limited) advises on every pick. The captions do not label speakers; reasoning and ideas credit the guest or host only where the content makes it clear, otherwise both.
event: FRA live pod on Arena, recorded about 24 hours after release (the guest: 'the set has been out barely 24 hours'); best-of-three ('this is going to be best of three, so if we see the sideboard cards, we can actually take them'); Premier / Traditional not named on screen
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/XSY4dH0hZ8Y (banner and pack grid strips every pick; pool at P2p1, P2p3, P2p14; the final deck builder at 1632 s); every pack list read from images that loaded, except the last card of pack 3 (only a tooltip seen, inferred); takes confirmed by the pool and the transcript; P2p7 was auto-picked by a game glitch and the card is unknown; transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected against the dataset; nothing past 27:20 read; the cut-off is 1640 s

colour_path.quote: We are extraordinarily incentivized to play green.
I think the rare is pretty strong. I think it is better than taking the second improviser.
we can kind of dabble into other colors.
I just feel like we are likely to be like green something splashing something.
I think you should take Twisted Fates.
green green red and maybe splashing like vigor bloom charm or last gasp or whatever.

colour_path.main: GR + Vigorbloom Charm / Warrior's Blades splash (one Plains, one Dedicated Commons)
colour_path.quote: we're already kind of inclined to splash the charm.

picks.reasoning: Verdant Kraken is the slam-dunk first pick for both; if it were not there the guest would take Mindseeker Oculus, the best common, because the uncommons (Koth of the Homestead needs the counter / life-gain plan, Winter the sacrifice plan) do not pull him into their colours.

considered.Mindseeker Oculus: guest: the pick if the rare were not in the pack; host takes Oculus nearly every time he sees it
considered.Koth of the Homestead: good only in the plus-one-counter life-gain deck
considered.Winter, Tormented Loner: good only in the black sacrifice deck

quotes: It's sort of a dealer's choice, I think I would lean towards the Mindseeker Oculus ... that's the best common that we've got here.

picks.reasoning: Konstrari Improviser, the red-green card that fits the Kraken: the guest does not generally want to play it on two but it is the best card that goes with what they have; he declines Fatehold Chronologist (flexible, but it could move them off the Kraken) and says Edgar is good only in black-white and Arni, the blue one, is worth killing.

considered.Fatehold Chronologist: guest: a common he likes; host: great when his opponents played it, never found time to use the ability; not taken to avoid moving off the Kraken
considered.Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord: good if you end up black-white
considered.Arni, Humble Scribe: impressed him from the other side of the table

quotes: Verdant Kraken is really good. We are extraordinarily incentivized to play green. I don't think that I want to take like a hidden power and take chronologist there and potentially move off of drafting the Kraken.

picks.reasoning: Arcane Amphisbaena over Stingerquill Charm, the pack's best card: the guest finds it very similar to the previous pack and likes the Amphisbaena more than the Improviser; red-black is the deck he is most dubious of, and the host agrees.

considered.Stingerquill Charm: guest: maybe the best card in the pack; red-black is his least favourite deck

quotes: Red Black is probably the deck I am most dubious of, like least excited.

picks.reasoning: Marwyn, the Preserver: a really good two-drop with synergy with Jace's surveil into the graveyard and with Something Worth Saving; guest favours green ramp with red as its best partner, and notes Way of the Mentor is best in green-white lifegain.

considered.Wrath of the Bloodmane: very good, would pair with green ramp and red

picks.plan: Green ramp, red likely the pair.
quotes: I would just take Marwyn here. It's a really good two drop. It has synergy with surveilling for lands into the bin from Jace.

picks.reasoning: Ajani's Anguish fifth pick: they both call it wild; the rare is better than taking the second Improviser. They note seeing about ten Arnis so far: bad pairs (the same pair repeated) are a bald spot in the packs.
quotes: I think the rare is pretty strong. I think it is better than taking the second improviser.

picks.reasoning: Last Gasp over Pompous Battlemage and Gallia: black-green is still possible but they have one red card; Gallia, the Merrymaker is not a good card (ground two/ones are not where it's at).

considered.Gallia, the Merrymaker: not good; ground two-ones are not where it is at (host: only strong when an opponent paired it with a big flier)

picks.plan: Green, red or black second colour.
quotes: I don't think Gallia of the Merry Maker is a good card. I think ground two ones are not where it's at.

picks.reasoning: Vigorbloom Charm: nothing in the pack is better than the green cards they have; green is a little dry but should be open in pack 2, and a Vigorbloom Charm at pick seven hopefully shows green-white is open.
quotes: this vigor bloom charm pick seven hopefully is indicative of green white being open, which would be a welcome place to be.

picks.reasoning: Loot, the Nexus out of a pack with Extended Absence, Wrath, Warrior's Blades and Loot: the host wants to wait and see rather than get pushed off red or black by taking a removal spell this late.
quotes: I kind of want to take loot because I just don't feel confident that like we take a red card, we might get pushed off red.

picks.reasoning: Edgar, Moonlit Sovereign over Silence the Echo: the host has not played it but read it from an opponent; with a bunch of green cards they can dabble in other colours or splash red, and the Improviser helps find a red source.
quotes: I feel like we just have like a bunch of green cards and then like we can kind of dabble into other colors.

picks.reasoning: Rank Rat: the guest thought discard would not be good because flashback and Jace-token card draw are everywhere, but it has felt very good each time it was cast against him.
quotes: I thought rat wasn't going to be good ... but it's felt very good every time it's been cast against me.

picks.reasoning: Theorix Annex (blue-black land) late: take the land, you never know when you find something; a good general rule is to take the lands when you need them.
quotes: That's a good like general rule to just take the lands when you when you need.

picks.reasoning: Something Worth Saving, which gets much better with a Verdant Kraken because finding it feels amazing.
quotes: this card gets exponentially better when you have a card like Verdant Kraken because every time you find it, you just feel like amazing

picks.reasoning: Blazing Crescendo over Arni, Renowned Champion: doesn't matter to either of them.
quotes: I don't Yeah, doesn't matter to me.

picks.reasoning: Last card, Mountain, auto-picked.

Fblthp, Knows the Way (green): they are likely green something splashing something, and it is perfect for that; the guest has loved Fblthp and thinks the sweet spot is splashing so he can be a 3/2 (domain). He also notes the person passed to likely took a white card (Way of the Healer) because both Fblthps and the white way were in the pair set.
quotes: I'm definitely drawn towards the green Fblthp. I just feel like we are likely to be like green something splashing something.

picks.reasoning: Tarmogoyf over a Fblthp, Impossibly Lost, Hunter's Axe and the second Improviser: they do not discuss the take; the pool shows Tarmogoyf here.

A second Fblthp, Knows the Way over the two green two-drops; Jace's Machinations, Plan for All Outcomes and Mindseeker Oculus in the pack. The guest suspects the player passing in pack 1 was blue (no good blue cards) and now blue is coming; the person next to them could not get into blue.
quotes: I'm suspecting the person passing to us in pack one was playing blue because we didn't see like any good blue cards and now they're coming this way.

picks.reasoning: Twisted Fates, pretty nuts according to the guest even though it is not black-black enough for a green-black splash; the host likes Mind Meanderer too. They have Vigorbloom Charm for a green-white splash.
picks.plan: Green with a splash (black or white).
quotes: I think you should take Twisted Fates. I think Twisted Fates is pretty nuts.

picks.reasoning: Fatehold Chronologist for a green-white shell; Paradox Shaper would be for going back to green-black, but they do not necessarily want that.

considered.Paradox Shaper: for green-black; both have stacked their decks with it

quotes: I like chronologist here.

picks.reasoning: Arcane Amphisbaena over Tinybones and Titanbones: the guest has not played Titanbones; they do not have much life gain, and the host recalls a Titanbones discard to gain three that saved an opponent.

considered.Titanbones, Towering Heart: guest has not played with it; host saw it punish an attack

quotes: I think I would be inclined to take a bayana but uh I have not played with titan bones.

picks.reasoning: taken: unknown (see below). Rescue Girl, First Responder was the card he wanted (the host hovered it and says it is 'so good' with Fblthp, Ajani's Anguish and their deck); the game glitched and the pick was auto-selected before he could take it. Which card was auto-picked is unknown: the host says he thinks it took a basic land; nothing in the pool or the pack can be matched to this pick.

considered.Rescue Girl, First Responder: the intended pick; good with Fblthp and Ajani's Anguish; would have been splashed

quotes: Oh rescue girl. Rescue girl so good.
The game just glitched out. We getting autopicked.
I took a basic land for us in that pack. So, I don't know what happened there exactly.

picks.reasoning: Formidable Commons from a pack of Karn, Sphinx's Approach, Undulating Witness, Rank Rat, Battlecarver, Inspired Tethermage and the land, straight after the glitch; no spoken reasoning for the take, which is confirmed from the pool.
Tam's Resistance: 'take the Tam's resistance' right after the glitch, over Mindseeker Oculus, Rampart Hunter and Tether Technician.
quotes: Take the Tam's resistance. Yeah, probably.

picks.reasoning: Hunter's Axe over Yargle and a second Twinned Vision; no spoken comment (the pick tag is on Hunter's Axe and the pool confirms it).
Academic Ascent over Fblthp, Impossibly Lost, Theorix Metamage and an Island; no spoken comment; the pool at P2p14 confirms it.
Kiora of Salt and Sand; no spoken comment; the pool confirms it.
Tether Technician over Graft Surgeon; no spoken comment; the pool confirms it.
Last card, Sphinx's Approach, auto-selected.

Kiora of Fire and Ashes over Way of the Wildspeaker: pretty nuts, especially with Fblthp to hit land drops; they can be green with red as the second colour, and she is a good ramp target. Way of the Wildspeaker is what the guest would take otherwise.

considered.Way of the Wildspeaker: guest: the pick if Kiora were not there

quotes: Kiora is pretty nuts and I think is probably worth taking here.
I think Kiora is just too good of a ramp target.

picks.reasoning: Bestial Incursion over Way of the Warlord and the black kill spell: a nice mid-range and late-game threat, they have a little self-mill from surveils, and green is the one colour they know they are playing while the second is undecided.

considered.Way of the Warlord: in the pack (wheels, taken at pick ten)

quotes: I kind of like the bestial incursion. It's just like a nice little not like exactly top end. It's like a mid-range threat and a late game threat.

picks.reasoning: Fulminous Forte: 'now I'm ready' to pick red; green-green-red, maybe splashing Vigorbloom Charm or Last Gasp. They would have splashed Rescue Girl if they had it.
picks.plan: Green-red; splash Charm or Last Gasp.
quotes: I think now I'm ready. We take the fulminous forte here.
green green red and maybe splashing like vigor bloom charm or last gasp or whatever.

picks.reasoning: Awaken the Inferno (basic landcycler) over Ghalta the Immovable: a good Awaken the Inferno deck; the guest calls Ghalta fine, just a five-mana 8/8 trample that does not feel busted, and takes the landcycler.

considered.Ghalta the Immovable: guest: fine, just a five mana 8/8 trample, not busted

quotes: I would take the Land Cycler. Yeah, this card's quite good.

picks.reasoning: A second Konstrari Improviser over a third Arcane Amphisbaena: it gives more ramp.
quotes: I think I would take second improviser over the third snake. Just gives us some more ramp stuff.

picks.reasoning: Wrath of the Bloodmane over Heartstring Puller and Traxos, Academy Guardian: they need the removal and would never take the Puller over one of the red removal spells; Awaken the Inferno and the two-mana deal-three are also good.

considered.Heartstring Puller: looks better than it plays; they would never take it over a red removal spell

quotes: I think Heartstring Puller looks better than it actually plays out ... I would never take it over one of the red removal spells.

picks.reasoning: A second Something Worth Saving: this deck is going to be pretty good at finding Kraken; with two Fblthps it is easy to splash, but they lack a good splash target.
quotes: I feel like this deck is going to be pretty good at finding Kraken.

picks.reasoning: Way of the Mind Sculptor, the blue card: not crazy as a splash because the deck has a lot of ramp but not a lot of card draw; chosen over the green card (Flourishing Grapple) and Clash of Elements.

considered.Flourishing Grapple: the green sideboard card; they prefer the blue Way

picks.plan: Green-red with a possible blue splash.
quotes: Way of the Mind Sculptor isn't crazy as a splash. Like you have a lot of ramp but not a lot of card draw.

picks.reasoning: Warrior's Blades: could be a fine splash, they are already inclined to splash the Vigorbloom Charm for interaction, and with a bunch of little guys the buff would be good.
picks.plan: Green-red with a white splash (Charm, Blades).
quotes: I like warriors blades and we're already kind of inclined to splash the charm.

picks.reasoning: Way of the Warlord over Way of the Mentor: a little extra synergy with the Way of the Mind Sculptor, the two Amphisbaenas and Tam's Resistance; they say it is the kind of card that could start in the sideboard.
quotes: All right, I take Way of the Warlord. Get a little bit extra synergy with the Way of the Mind Sculptor.

picks.reasoning: Twinned Vision over Wrecking Gecko: it solves the problem of having a ton of mana and needing something to do with it, and helps against flood.
quotes: Twin Vision is so good. Like again, it solves the problem of like you're going to have a ton of mana and hopeful you need stuff to do with it.

picks.reasoning: Dedicated Commons, the land, over Divining Duelist and Sureshot Sower: it is not essential but helps with Warrior's Blades and the Vigorbloom Charm.
quotes: Take the land here. I don't think this card's essential. And it helps us with our warriors blades. And our vigor bloom charm.

picks.reasoning: Marwyn, the Clearcutter over a Mountain: called 'just a Savannah Lions', but it works with the other Marwyn and Fblthp can turn extra lands into cards; the host got it with two cards left.
quotes: It's just a Savannah Lions.
It works well with the other Marwin that we have.

pack_cards: unreadable (last card only seen as a tooltip text, 'Put a +1/+1 counter on each of one or two target creatures. Flashback'; Predictive Preparations by elimination from the pick-6 pack)
picks.reasoning: Last card auto-selected; only a tooltip of the card was visible (Predictive Preparations by elimination).
